req.title: Reject wrong method on /post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than POST on /post.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /post must return HTTP 405 for any method other than POST. We need: (1) a positive test confirming POST returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD return exactly 405, and (3) boundary tests covering the method-set boundary (methods adjacent to POST in the allowed-methods list). Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (200 vs 405), testing both sides of the allowed/rejected boundary, and verifying the Allow header content where Flask sets it.

tests.name: test_post_method_returns_200
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send HTTP POST to /post with no body
expected: Response body is JSON containing keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: POST is the only allowed method; it must succeed with 200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_method_returns_200():
    r = client.post('/post')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data

test_post_method_returns_200()

preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: HTTP 200 (Flask handles OPTIONS automatically for registered routes)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: OPTIONS is the boundary between auto-handled and rejected methods; Flask returns 200 with Allow header listing POST

client = app.test_client()

def test_options_on_post_endpoint_not_405():
    r = client.options('/post')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    allow_header = r.headers.get('Allow', '')
    assert 'POST' in allow_header

tests.name: test_post_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send HTTP POST to /post with Content-Type application/json and a JSON body
expected: Response JSON contains 'json' key with the posted object
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: POST with a body must succeed with 200 and echo the json field
tests.executable:
import json
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key():
    payload = {"key": "value"}
    r = client.post(
        '/post',
        data=json.dumps(payload),
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['json'] == {"key": "value"}

test_post_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key()

tests.name: test_405_status_code_is_not_200_or_404
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: All non-POST methods return exactly 405, not 200, not 404, not 400
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: Mutation resilience — assert exact 405 and explicitly assert it is not 200/404/400 to catch constant-mutation operators
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_405_status_code_is_not_200_or_404():
    methods = [
        client.get, client.put, client.patch, client.delete
    ]
    for method_fn in methods:
        r = method_fn('/post')
        assert r.status_code == 405
        assert r.status_code != 200
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 400

test_405_status_code_is_not_200_or_404()
